newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. African court approves new constitution.
newsitem.headline: S. African court approves new constitution.

text.p: South Africa's senior court on Wednesday ratified a final post-apartheid constitution that will cement the transition from white rule to democracy.

Constitutional Court President Arthur Chaskalson said the text adopted by legislators in October after more than two years of negotiation was in line with principles agreed between the country's present and former rulers.
President Nelson Mandela is expected to sign the constitution at a ceremony marking International Human Rights Day next Tuesday and to order it implemented from the first of January next year.
The constitution guarantees equality to all citizens following more than three centuries of exclusive white rule that skewed the distribution of wealth, land and social services.
It includes a Bill of Rights and entrenches the independence of fiscal and social watchdogs and the central Reserve Bank.
